overview: Uganda's femtech and women's health innovation scene is anchored in maternal and reproductive health, driven by high maternal mortality and low contraceptive access. Homegrown ventures like M-SCAN (portable ultrasound), CHIL AI Lab (AI cervical and breast cancer screening) and Rocket Health (telemedicine) sit alongside regional e-commerce player Kasha, which serves Uganda among several African markets. Government policy through the RMNCAH Sharpened Plan II and FP2030 commitments, plus accelerators like DSW's POWER programme and UNICEF Femtech Ventures, shape a growing but still grant-dependent ecosystem centred on Kampala.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent milestones span product launches, accelerator cohorts and investor moves relevant to Ugandan women's health founders.

items.text: Five35 Ventures, a pan-African female-focused VC and a Kasha investor, secured an anchor commitment from the Mastercard Foundation Africa Growth Fund to expand gender-lens investing across Africa.
UNICEF launched Femtech Ventures with a first cohort of 11 frontier-tech startups across Africa and Asia, selected from over 1,100 applications, more than half from Africa.
DSW and Action 4 Health Uganda launched the POWER Accelerator 2024-25 cohort to grow women-led family planning and SRHR startups to 32 total by 2025.
CHIL Femtech Center unveiled a new AI feature to address medical challenges in Africa, extending its tele-oncology and self-collection cervical cancer screening.
NeoSave, a Ugandan neonatal-care healthtech, was named among African finalists in the 2024 ASME ISHOW global hardware innovation accelerator.
Three Uganda female-led health startups (CHIL AI Lab, Peleyta Health, Mama Ope Medicals) were selected for WiNFUND funding.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: National policy centres on cutting maternal deaths and lifting contraceptive access, providing the frame for women's health innovation.

items.text: RMNCAH Sharpened Plan II (2022/23-2026/27) set interventions to expand family planning, strengthen emergency obstetric and newborn care, and institutionalize maternal and perinatal death surveillance.
Uganda renewed FP2030 commitments, pledging to raise modern contraceptive prevalence to 39.6% and cut unmet need to 15% by 2025.
National Development Plan III set a target to reduce the maternal mortality ratio from 311 to 211 by 2025.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Accelerators, hubs and dedicated women's workspaces are building support infrastructure around Kampala.

items.text: DSW established a Women's Business Hub at its Bonita Training Centre as a training space and workspace for new female-led SRHR startups.

UNICEF Femtech Ventures (2025-2030) offers up to USD 100,000 equity-free per startup for AI, data science and blockchain solutions in maternal and reproductive health, backed by Sweden and Temasek Foundation.
POWER pilot's first phase produced startups offering contraceptive information, HIV self-testing kits, period wellness products and mental health support via ICT platforms.
Innovation Village and Outbox Hub anchor Kampala's tech ecosystem, offering incubation across sectors including e-health tech.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: A mix of homegrown startups, hubs, government and NGOs make up Uganda's women's health innovation landscape.

items.name: M-SCAN
items.note: Low-cost USB portable ultrasound for prenatal care in rural and peri-urban areas; 9,400+ scans performed

items.name: CHIL AI Lab / CHIL Femtech Center
items.note: AI tele-oncology platform for self-collection cervical and breast cancer screening; founded by Shamim Nabuuma Kaliisa

items.name: Rocket Health
items.note: Kampala telemedicine and last-mile care with 24/7 teleconsults, medicine delivery and diagnostics

items.name: WinSenga
items.note: Smartphone-based fetal heart-rate monitor from Makerere University students (Cipher256)

items.name: Kasha
items.note: Women's health, hygiene and self-care e-commerce operating in Uganda among several African markets

items.name: NeoSave Technologies
items.note: Neonatal-care healthtech; 2024 ASME ISHOW finalist and women-led health innovation cohort member

items.name: Peleyta Health
items.note: Digital healthcare micro-savings and lending fintech for low-income earners; WiNFUND selectee

items.name: Mama Ope Medicals
items.note: Health-device startup selected in 2023 WiNFUND cohort of female-led Ugandan health ventures

items.name: Uganda Ministry of Health
items.note: Coordinates the national digital health ecosystem and RMNCAH / family planning strategy

items.name: DSW / Action 4 Health Uganda
items.note: Run the POWER Accelerator and Women's Business Hub for SRHR women entrepreneurs

items.name: The Innovation Village
items.note: National ICT innovation hub with multi-city branches supporting Ugandan startups

items.name: Outbox Hub
items.note: Kampala incubator supporting startups in fintech, e-health tech and agriculture

items.name: Days for Girls Uganda

items.name: HealthTech Hub Africa
items.note: Pan-African accelerator profiling and supporting Ugandan healthtech ventures including M-SCAN
